status: Three authorized exposition revisions completed and checked
reviewer: Preparing Codex assistant; not an independent reviewer

changes.change: Define Phi(x) as the limit of n^(-1) log R_n(n(7+x)) along even n for fixed x>0. Explain its role in bounding the positive tail, show the numerator and denominator gamma-product identities, and then derive the existing profile by Stirling. Identify x=0 as a continuous extension of the profile.

Explain the unique possible exceptional pole group before the valuation calculation. Introduce the denominator bases x_k, prove that at most one can exceed the prime-power allowance, and use the numerator-zero identity to prove integrality in the two cases.
Replace the ambiguous shorter-list comparison by a list omitting beta(2).

exposition_assessment.before_the_profile: The reader knows that t measures distance past the last zero, that x=t/n is held fixed, and what the exponential rate Phi measures.
exposition_assessment.before_maximization: The role of the maximum and the later need to control the whole infinite tail are explicit.
exposition_assessment.before_valuation_algebra: The reader knows why only one pole group can be exceptional and how a zero relation transfers integrality to it.
exposition_assessment.scope: Targeted authoring review against the human-reading principles; no independent reader assessment is claimed.

added_argument_checks.symbolic_review: The numerator and denominator gamma identities follow from the gamma recurrence with lengths 18n and n+1. The denominator scale is 4^(n+1), and its upper argument is (11n+t)/4+1. The pre-existing profile formula is unchanged.
added_argument_checks.group_scope: All relevant odd finite-sum indices for n=2,4,6,8 and b=1,2,3, at all primes below 101. This supports the general difference-and-valuation proof; it does not replace it.
added_argument_checks.numeric_scope: Floating-point diagnostics of the displayed gamma arguments; not an exact certificate.

preservation_checks.grouped_constant_proof: Same coefficient bound and numerator-zero identity; reorganized around uniqueness of an exceptional denominator base.
